family: Classic published trading systems and author methods
notes: Report: /home/user/claude-workspace/research/families/classic_systems_authors.md. WebSearch budget was exhausted by the parent workflow after 6 searches; the sweep was completed with ~70 direct fetches (mesasoftware PDFs, oxfordstrat, Capstone product pages, demark.com, ProRealCode, elitetrader/nexusfi excerpts, x-trader.net, tradingsetupsreview, mql5, luxalgo, bettersystemtrader, KJ Trading). quantifiedstrategies.com (bot wall), Unger Academy (captcha), Scribd and web.archive.org were unreachable; rules taken from the books themselves are marked [book], standard objective readings of vague sources [interp]. Key findings: (1) almost nothing in this family has a modern net-of-cost OOS record on ES/NQ/GC intraday; oxfordstrat multi-decade tests rate Crabel narrow-range ORB and Williams Oops "C" (gross-positive, marginal after $50 RT) and wide-range "D" (PF 0.74). (2) The only 2024-2026 year-by-year numbers (Capstone/David Bean, hypothetical, no slippage) show NQ gap-continuation and open-range day trades still profitable every year (2025 weakest) while ES gap-fill (09:32 fade) and ES 09:31 long-reversal systems went flat/negative in 2024-2026: bias toward NQ continuation after the open, ES fades only with tight time stops. (3) Exit evidence is the most transferable: Davey's 567k-backtest study (40 futures, 2010-2020) found dollar targets > ATR targets, targets > stops, breakeven third, trailing/parabolic/chandelier worse, only indices and metals positive; Ehlers shows confirmation-based oscillator entries lose while anticipatory crossings win (daily S&P), and his bond tests give PF 1.7-2.1 at 53-57% wins. (4) Best-shaped candidates for Lucid: Crabel stretch ORB on NR4/ID/NR7 days with close confirmation; 80-20/Turtle-Soup prior-day-extreme re-entries; Williams volatility breakout with bond filter in micros; Momentum Pinball (daily LBR/RSI filter + first-hour ORB); ACD time-confirmation + failed-A wrapper; Ehlers roofing-filter anticipatory stochastic with adverse-excursion reversal; Capstone-style NQ gap continuation ($1,225 NQ stop = $122 MNQ). (5) Poor fits: Turtle entries, TD Sequential, KAMA/MAMA crossovers, Collins stop-less open-to-close holds, Ruggiero intermarket/report-day (needs calendar), Bandy multi-day equity reversion. Section 30 of the report lists seven concrete first parameter sets (F1-F7) and four filters for the backtest queue.

strategies.name: Original Turtle rules (System 1 20/10, System 2 55/20)
strategies.origin: Dennis/Eckhardt 1983-88; rules published by Curtis Faith (originalturtles.org / tradingblox.com PDF)
strategies.entry: N = 20-day Wilder-style average true range. S1: buy 1 tick above the 20-day high (sell below 20-day low); skip if the previous S1 breakout in that market was a winner (loser = moved 2N against before a profitable 10-day exit); 55-day breakout always taken. S2: 55-day breakout always. Add 1 unit each 1/2 N up to 4 units.
strategies.exit: Stop 2N from the latest entry (earlier units' stops raised 1/2 N on each add; whipsaw variant 1/2 N). S1 exits at the 10-day low/high, S2 at the 20-day low/high.
strategies.filters: Last-breakout-was-a-winner skip; position limits 4 units/market, 6 closely correlated, 10 loosely, 12 per direction.
strategies.parameters: Unit = 1% of equity / (N x $ per point); N length 20; 20/10 and 55/20 channels; 2N stop; 1/2 N pyramid step.
strategies.instruments: Diversified futures portfolio; on single-market ES/NQ since 2010 the 20-day breakout has been a documented loser
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily bars, multi-week holds (not day-trade)
strategies.claimed_performance: Turtle program ~80%/yr 1983-88 on a 40+ market portfolio; Trading Blox forum re-tests positive through the 2000s; no intraday evidence
strategies.prop_fit: Poor as published (overnight holds forbidden). Reusable: N-based micro sizing, the skip-after-a-winner filter for intraday ORBs, 55 vs 20 bar intraday Donchian as a test-only variant.

strategies.name: Larry Williams Oops! gap reversal
strategies.origin: Larry Williams, How I Made One Million Dollars (1973); Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999)
strategies.entry: Buy: today's open < yesterday's low; buy stop at yesterday's low (a tick above) filled only if price trades back up through it. Sell: open > yesterday's high; sell stop at yesterday's high. Gap bar cannot confirm itself (mql5/forge version requires a completed bar closing back through the level, validity 3 bars, minimum gap size).
strategies.exit: Stop at the gap bar's extreme (today's low for longs); Williams: bail-out at first profitable open or dollar stop; day-trade version: flat at the close (TradingView version trails the current day's low, force-flat last bar, no target).
strategies.filters: Williams [book]: trade day of week, T-bonds closed higher than 5 days ago for S&P buys, buys only after a down close.
strategies.parameters: Entry offset 1-2 ticks; stop = gap extreme (0.3-0.6 x ATR typical); target prior close or 1 x ATR; orders active 09:30-11:30 ET in intraday adaptations.
strategies.instruments: S&P, bonds originally; tested on 42 US futures (oxfordstrat), XAUUSD (mql5)
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily setup, intraday execution; RTH 09:30-16:00 ET, flat by close
strategies.claimed_performance: oxfordstrat Bull Oops 42 futures 1980-2011 daily, time exits 1-40 days, 6xATR stop: rated C (gross-positive, no table). mql5 XAUUSD daily 2022-2026: 8 trades, +$523 on $10k (meaningless). Unger Academy 2025 test exists but is captcha-walled.
strategies.prop_fit: Objective, small stop, low frequency (open outside prior range ~15-25% of NQ days); fits consistency rule with prior-close target. Special case of the open-outside-range fade statistic.

strategies.name: Larry Williams Smash Day (naked and hidden)
strategies.origin: Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999) [book]; ProRealCode forum implementation
strategies.entry: Naked buy smash day = a day closing below the previous day's low; next day buy stop at the smash day's high (valid that day only). Naked sell = close above the previous day's high; sell stop at the smash day's low. Hidden smash buy: close in the bottom 25% of the range without taking out the prior low; buy above its high next day [book, paraphrased]. ProRealCode: If Close < Low[1] then buy at High stop, filter High[1] < High[n].
strategies.exit: Stop below the smash day low (longs); Williams bail-out at first profitable open or flat at close; ProRealCode uses fixed SL/TP in ticks.
strategies.filters: TDW and bond-trend filter (Williams); High[1] < High[n], n = 5-30 (ProRealCode).
strategies.parameters: Hidden smash threshold 25% of range; n filter 5-30; SL 0-600 pips optimized in forum version.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily pattern, next-day stop entry; day-trade exit at close
strategies.claimed_performance: Book tables only (S&P/bonds 1980s-90s); ProRealCode thread has code, no stats.
strategies.prop_fit: One-day failed-breakdown reversal executed as a stop at the prior day's high; risk = smash-day range (often > 1 x ATR on NQ) so 2-5 micros; low frequency.

strategies.name: Larry Williams volatility breakout (open + k x prior range) with bond/TDW filters
strategies.origin: Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading ch. 4 [book]; also in Kaufman, Trading Systems and Methods
strategies.entry: Buy stop at today's open + k x yesterday's range (or larger of last 1-3 ranges / true range); sell stop at open - k x range. k market-specific, mostly 0.5-0.8 (standard k = 0.6).
strategies.exit: Opposite stop (reverse) or dollar stop; exit at the close (day trade) or bail-out at the first profitable open.
strategies.filters: Take buys only when T-bonds closed higher than 5 (or 10) days ago; trade-day-of-week tables; buys after a down close, sells after an up close.
strategies.parameters: k 0.5-0.8; bond lookback 5-10 days; TDW per market; dollar stop $150-250 per micro recommended.
strategies.instruments: S&P, bonds (book); ES/NQ/MES/MNQ for our test
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily range, stop entry during RTH, flat at close
strategies.claimed_performance: Book in-sample S&P tables 1982-1998 report 80%+ profitable with the bond filter [book]; modern ORB literature (Zarattini 2023/2024, Mesfin 2026) shows the generic open-plus-fraction-of-range edge is gross-positive but within slippage unless filtered.
strategies.prop_fit: One entry, hard stop, EOD exit. With k = 0.6 the NQ trigger is 150-240 pts from the open (triggers late/rarely); ES stop-and-reverse width is $3,000-5,000 per mini, so micros with a dollar stop instead of the full reverse. Bond filter codeable from Yahoo daily ZB.
strategies.data_requirements: Daily + 1-min OHLC; daily T-bond closes (Yahoo) for the filter

strategies.name: Williams %R oversold/overbought (10/14-period)
strategies.origin: Larry Williams (1973); formula per TradingView/ireallytrade.com
strategies.entry: %R = (HH(n) - C)/(HH(n) - LL(n)) x -100, n = 14 (Williams used 10). Standard intraday form [interp]: 5-min RTH, long when %R crosses up through -80 with daily close > 20-day SMA; short mirror through -20 in a downtrend. Momentum failure (fails to re-enter the zone) as a reversal signal.
strategies.exit: Exit when %R reaches -20 (longs) or at 15:55; stop 0.75 x ATR(14, 5-min).
strategies.filters: Daily trend filter (20-day SMA or bond filter).
strategies.parameters: n = 10 or 14; zones -80/-20 (Williams -90/-10).
strategies.timeframe_session: 5-min RTH bars 09:30-15:55 ET
strategies.claimed_performance: No independent backtest found; indicator-description sources only.
strategies.prop_fit: Many small mean-reversion trades fit the consistency rule, but Ehlers' evidence says confirmation-style oscillator entries lose to lag; prefer the anticipatory crossing (see Ehlers entry).

strategies.name: Turtle Soup and Turtle Soup Plus One (Street Smarts)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts (1995) ch. 1-2
strategies.entry: Buy: today makes a new 20-day low; the previous 20-day low must be >= 4 trading days old; buy stop 5-10 ticks above the previous 20-day low, good today only. Plus One: today's close at/below the previous 20-day low, buy stop placed the next day at that low. Intraday adaptation [interp]: 5-min RTH, level = prior-day low or 20-bar low (prior extreme >= 4 bars old), price breaks by >= 2 ticks then a bar closes back above -> buy stop 1 tick above the level.
strategies.exit: Stop 1 tick below today's low (Plus One: below the lower of the last two days' lows); re-enter once at the original price on day 1-2; take profits in 2-6 days with a trailing stop. Intraday: stop at the breakout extreme capped 0.5 x ATR, target 1 x ATR or VWAP, flat 15:55.
strategies.filters: Prior extreme >= 4 days/bars old; regime (works in rotational markets).
strategies.parameters: Lookback 20; entry offset 5-10 ticks; min age 4; ProRealCode M30 forex variant: 5-bar lows, EMA 21 > EMA 30, 3 x ATR(20) stop, 06:00-22:00.
strategies.instruments: Any futures; ES/NQ/GC for our test
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily setup, intraday execution; flat by 15:55 ET
strategies.claimed_performance: No statistics in the book; ProRealCode M30 forex test: positive long term but 'bad profit factor'; luxalgo: regime-dependent.
strategies.prop_fit: Good risk shape (stop at failed-break extreme 0.2-0.5 x ATR), low frequency; downside-break failures stronger than upside in 2023-2026.

strategies.name: 80-20s / 90-10s (Street Smarts, Taylor-Moore)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts ch. 3; Steve Moore statistics; mql5 implementation
strategies.entry: Buy: yesterday opened in the top 20% of its range and closed in the bottom 20% (90-10 variant: top/bottom 10%); today trades at least 5-15 ticks below yesterday's low; buy stop at yesterday's low. Sell: mirror at yesterday's high.
strategies.exit: Initial stop at today's low (high for shorts); trail; it is a day trade, exit by the close. Day-trade target: prior close or 1 x ATR.
strategies.filters: mql5: yesterday's range > 20-day average range; one trade per day; active 09:30-13:00 ET in intraday use.
strategies.parameters: Open/close zones 20% (or 10%); extension 5-15 ticks; optional TP multiple of the break.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily setup, next-session execution, flat at close
strategies.claimed_performance: Moore stat: close in top/bottom 10% -> 80-90% follow-through next morning but ~50% close beyond; mql5 2016 FX daily: 233 trades over ~6 years, marginal profitability, 'requires modernization'.
strategies.prop_fit: Rare, objective, tight risk, day trade by construction; best as an upgrade filter for the prior-day-extreme fade.

strategies.name: Momentum Pinball (LBR/RSI + first-hour range breakout)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts ch. 4 [book]; ProRealCode indicator
strategies.entry: LBR/RSI = 3-period RSI of the 1-day ROC (close - close[1]) on daily bars. Buy day: yesterday's LBR/RSI < 30; today let the first hour 09:30-10:30 ET form; buy stop above the first-hour high. Sell day: LBR/RSI > 70; sell stop below the first-hour low. Re-enter once if re-triggered after a stop.
strategies.exit: Stop at the first-hour low (a few ticks below); book: hold overnight if profitable at the close and exit next morning; day-trade version: flat 15:55; target 1 x first-hour range.
strategies.filters: Daily oscillator extreme (<30 / >70) defines direction; first-hour range defines risk.
strategies.parameters: RSI length 3 on ROC(1); thresholds 30/70 (ProRealCode indicator uses 14 and 40/60, a different parameterisation); first hour 60 min; stop cap 0.5 x ATR.
strategies.instruments: S&P, bonds originally; ES/NQ for test
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily filter + 60-min ORB, entries after 10:30 ET, flat 15:55
strategies.claimed_performance: No independent statistics; ORB component supported by modern IB/first-hour studies (~60-72% continuation with context filters).
strategies.prop_fit: At most one trade a day after the opening chaos, risk = first-hour range (ES 15-30 pts, NQ 80-200 -> micros), directional filter from prior days; drop the overnight hold.

strategies.name: Holy Grail (ADX > 30 rising + 20-EMA pullback)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts ch. 6; tradingsetupsreview codification
strategies.entry: 14-period ADX > 30 and rising; price retraces to the 20-period EMA (tradingsetupsreview uses SMA); buy stop at the high of the bar that touched the average (lower it to each new touching bar's high); shorts mirror with -DI dominant.
strategies.exit: Initial stop below the recent swing low; target the recent swing high (partial), trail the rest; cancel if ADX turns down; flat 15:55 intraday.
strategies.filters: ADX rising requirement; some sources use ADX > 20.
strategies.parameters: ADX 14, threshold 30, EMA 20.
strategies.timeframe_session: Any; 5-min ES/NQ RTH for our test (ADX needs ~30 bars of history)
strategies.claimed_performance: Book and tradingsetupsreview examples only; caveat that high ADX can mark exhaustion.
strategies.prop_fit: Pullback-in-trend entry with tight stop (4-8 ES pts on 5-min), ~50% WR, 1.2-1.5 R; acceptable in micros.

strategies.name: ADX Gapper (trend-filtered Oops)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts ch. 7 [book]
strategies.entry: ADX(14) > 30 (some summaries 20) with +DI > -DI; today opens below yesterday's low; buy stop at yesterday's low. Short mirror in a downtrend when the open is above yesterday's high.
strategies.exit: Stop at today's low; trail; exit at the close or next day; do not hold if the day closes below yesterday's low.
strategies.filters: Wilder trend filter removes counter-trend Oops trades.
strategies.parameters: ADX 14 > 30; entry at prior extreme.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily setup, intraday execution, flat at close
strategies.claimed_performance: Book only.
strategies.prop_fit: Same as Oops with lower frequency and better directional accuracy; small stop.

strategies.name: The Anti (stochastic hook, 7/10/3)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts ch. 8; roboforex parameters
strategies.entry: Slow stochastic 7,10,3. %D sets the short-term trend; %K hooks against %D for 3-4 bars (pullback) then hooks back in %D's direction; buy stop above the high of the hook bar (short mirror).
strategies.exit: Stop below the hook bar's low; held strictly one day / exit at the close.
strategies.filters: Trend-day filter recommended (fades badly on rotational days).
strategies.parameters: Stochastic 7,10,3; hook 3-4 bars.
strategies.timeframe_session: Any timeframe; 5-min RTH for our test
strategies.claimed_performance: Book examples only.
strategies.prop_fit: Pullback continuation with small stops and frequent signals; needs a trend filter.

strategies.name: Whiplash climax reversal (Street Smarts, standard interpretation)
strategies.origin: Connors & Raschke, Street Smarts part 3 ch. 9 [interp - book text not retrievable]
strategies.entry: Sell: Day 1 makes a new 20-day high; Day 2 trades above Day 1's high then closes below Day 1's low (outside reversal); Day 3 sell stop 1 tick below Day 2's low. Buy mirror after a new 20-day low.
strategies.exit: Stop 1 tick above Day 2's high; exit at Day 3 close or 2-day time stop.
strategies.filters: None published.
strategies.parameters: Lookback 20; 2-day time stop.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily pattern, next-day stop entry
strategies.claimed_performance: None; related oxfordstrat 'Reversal Patterns part 2' (42 futures 1980-2019, $50 RT): base PF 0.97, CAGR -0.4%, win 34.5%, rated C, positive only with 8:1 reward exits.
strategies.prop_fit: Low frequency, large stop, needs huge targets per oxfordstrat: wrong shape for the consistency rule. Low priority.

strategies.name: Crabel Opening Range Breakout with Stretch (and ORB II)
strategies.origin: Toby Crabel, Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout (1990); x-trader.net summaries; oxfordstrat tests
strategies.entry: Stretch = 10-day SMA of min(High-Open, Open-Low). Buy stop at Open + Stretch, sell stop at Open - Stretch; first fill is the position, the other order becomes the reversal/protective stop. Earlier triggers are better (first 10 min); cancel unfilled orders after 5-10 min (ORB II: a wide-range directional bar in the first 5 minutes is itself the entry).
strategies.exit: Liquidate at the close; oxfordstrat swing variant: 10-day time exit, 6 x ATR(20) stop, stretch x2.
strategies.filters: Trade after Inside Day, NR4/NR7 (incl. dojis), Bull/Bear Hook, ID/NR4; avoid after wide-spread days; S&P gap rules (bigger gaps continue; counter-gap ORBs minimally profitable; bonds/gold behave opposite).
strategies.parameters: Stretch lookback 10 (multiplier 1.0 Crabel, 2.0 oxfordstrat); entry window 09:30-10:30 ET; exit 15:55; recommended target 0.5 x 14-day ATR.
strategies.instruments: S&P, bonds (Crabel); 42 US futures (oxfordstrat); Nasdaq (Unger test, blocked)
strategies.timeframe_session: Day trade, RTH 09:30-16:00 ET
strategies.claimed_performance: Crabel S&P tables 1982-89: 60-71% profitable at close after NR4/ID setups (one table 203 trades, 71%, avg win $343 / loss $289). oxfordstrat Narrow Range N-day (1980-2013) and NR7 (1980-2016): rated C, 'not currently tradeable without additional rules' after $50 RT; Wide Range: D, net -$873k, CAGR -5.1%, Sharpe -1.45, MDD 88%, win 23.8%, PF 0.74.
strategies.prop_fit: Best-shaped ORB in the family: ES stretch ~5-10 pts (NQ 25-60) so stop = 2x stretch is $500-1,000 per ES mini -> MES/MNQ; add a 0.5-1.0 x ATR target to cut EOD fat tails; NR4/ID/NR7 filter gives 2-4 setups a week across ES/NQ/GC.

strategies.name: Crabel ID/NR4 and NR7 pattern-bar breakouts
strategies.origin: Crabel (1990); tradingsetupsreview and mql5 NR7 ORB EA codifications
strategies.entry: NR4 = narrowest range of last 4; NR7 = of last 7; ID = high < prior high and low > prior low; ID/NR4 = both; Bull Hook = NRx day opening above prior high and closing below prior close. Buy stop 1 tick above the pattern bar's high, sell stop 1 tick below its low; mql5 EA: compression zone = 7-bar window high/low, 1-pip break.
strategies.exit: Stop at the opposite end of the pattern bar; cancel if the next bar does not trigger; flat at session end (EA: no new trades on the last candle).
strategies.filters: tradingsetupsreview: last 7 bars entirely above/below the 20-EMA; avoid consecutive NR7s (congestion).
strategies.parameters: NR length 4 or 7; EMA 20; intraday bar size 5/15/30 min (mql5 recommends M30).
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily or intraday pattern bars; RTH execution, flat at close
strategies.claimed_performance: Crabel's tables; oxfordstrat NR7 C-rated (positive gross, fails $50 costs on swing exits); EA has no stats.
strategies.prop_fit: Tight objective risk (pattern-bar range); setup filter for the stretch ORB; 15/30-min NR7 breakouts give 1-3 trades a day.

strategies.name: Mark Fisher ACD (A-up/A-down, C levels, pivot range)
strategies.origin: Mark B. Fisher, The Logical Trader (2002); elitetrader ACD-thread excerpts; TradingView Session OR A-Lines script
strategies.entry: OR = first N minutes (Fisher: CL 45 min, S&P ~20 min pit era; modern ES/NQ 5-15 min from 09:30 ET). A = 20-25% of a 5- or 10-day ATR (CL example A 0.08, C 0.13; TradingView defaults A 0.5% of OR, C 1-2%). Long when price holds above OR high + A for a time window (standard: half the OR length); C-down reversal short at OR low - C after a failed A-up, stop above the OR. Only the first fade/A of the day has edge.
strategies.exit: Stop back inside the OR (OR high for longs) or the confirmation-bar low on strong days; 'minimize risk by time, not by price'; flat at close.
strategies.filters: Pivot range = (H+L+C)/3 +/- |pivot - (H+L)/2|; narrow pivot ranges (3 consecutive) precede volatile days; 3-day rolling pivot bias.
strategies.parameters: OR 5-45 min; A = 0.2-0.25 x ATR(5-10 day); C ~1.5-2 x A; confirmation ~half OR length.
strategies.timeframe_session: Intraday from the session open; RTH
strategies.claimed_performance: Anecdotal; Fisher: 5-min OR is the high or low of the day ~15-18% of the time for CL; thread claims ~75% wins on longer-term confirmed trades; no public backtest.
strategies.prop_fit: Risk-control wrapper (time confirmation, failed-A reversal, first-A only) that fixes wick-break and re-trigger ORB failures; A = 0.2 x ATR on ES = 12-16 pts so OR-low stops risk $1,250-2,000 per mini -> micros or confirmation-bar stop.

strategies.name: Kaufman KAMA with std-dev filter and Efficiency Ratio regime filter
strategies.origin: Perry Kaufman, Smarter Trading (1995); Trading Systems and Methods ch. 17 (pp. 436-438 cited by Ehlers) [book]
strategies.entry: ER(10) = |C - C[10]| / sum of 10 one-bar absolute changes; SC = [ER x (0.6667 - 0.0645) + 0.0645]^2; KAMA = KAMA[1] + SC x (C - KAMA[1]). Buy when KAMA turns up by more than filter = 1.0 x stdev of 1-bar KAMA changes over 20 bars (0.1-1.0 suggested); or price crosses KAMA.
strategies.exit: Exit/sell when KAMA turns down by more than the filter.
strategies.filters: ER > ~0.3 = trending (allow breakouts), ER < 0.3 = noisy (fade or stand aside).
strategies.parameters: ER length 10; fast 2, slow 30; filter 1.0 x stdev(20).
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily; intraday use as a regime filter
strategies.claimed_performance: Kaufman's own daily tests (1990s); no modern intraday ES evidence.
strategies.prop_fit: Lagging trend follower, bad shape intraday; valuable as a cheap objective regime filter (ER(10, daily) > 0.3 gate for breakout strategies).

strategies.name: DeMark TD Setup (9) and TD Sequential Countdown (13)
strategies.origin: Tom DeMark, The New Science of Technical Analysis (1994); demark.com Sequential page
strategies.entry: Price flip (close < close[4] after close > close[4]) then Buy Setup = 9 consecutive closes < close 4 bars earlier (Sell Setup mirror); perfected if low of bar 8 or 9 < lows of bars 6 and 7; TDST = setup extreme. Countdown from bar 9: 13 non-consecutive closes <= low 2 bars earlier (buy); 13's low must be <= close of countdown bar 8 else deferred; cancelled by an opposite setup or TDST violation; recycled if an overlapping setup reaches 22 bars or 100-200% of the prior setup range. Standard rule [interp]: buy at the close of setup 9 or countdown 13.
strategies.exit: Stop = lowest low of the setup minus that bar's true range (risk level); target TDST; reversal expected within 12 bars of the 13.
strategies.filters: Perfection, TDST, cancellation/recycle rules.
strategies.parameters: Setup 9 vs close[4]; countdown 13 vs low/high[2]; 12-bar validity.
strategies.timeframe_session: Any; on 5-min RTH a 9-count takes 45 min, a 13 takes hours (0-2 signals/day)
strategies.claimed_performance: No independent ES/NQ test found; academic tests mostly crypto/equities, mixed.
strategies.prop_fit: Rare exhaustion entries against the trend; poor on trend days. Usable only as a do-not-chase filter.

strategies.name: Kevin Davey Strategy Factory: published price patterns and the 567k-backtest exit study
strategies.origin: Kevin Davey, Building Winning Algorithmic Trading Systems (2014); kjtradingsystems.com articles
strategies.entry: 15 published patterns, e.g. count up/down closes over BCount bars and go long if more ups and close < close[pullback]; short when consecutive up closes >= BCount and close > close[PCount]; outside/inside bar sequences with momentum direction; morning/evening doji star with 10-bar momentum (90-min mini S&P sample). Mini S&P strategy fully disclosed only to course members.
strategies.exit: Exit study (40 futures, 60-min to daily, 2010-2020, 5 entries x 15 exits): stop-and-reverse best, dollar target second, breakeven third; dollar exits > ATR exits; targets > stops; trailing/parabolic/chandelier/indicator exits underperform.
strategies.filters: Walk-forward, Monte Carlo on OOS, limited parameters, no re-optimising after losses.
strategies.parameters: BCount, PCount, pullback bars (non-optimized samples).
strategies.instruments: 40 futures; samples on SI, FC, ZF, CL, LH, NK, YM, NG, HG, EC, JY, MP, HO, ES
strategies.timeframe_session: 60-min to daily
strategies.claimed_performance: Pattern article: sample equity curves only. Exit study: only metals and stock indices had positive average returns. Mini S&P strategy: $121k+ hypothetical OOS per contract over 5 years (rules not public).
strategies.prop_fit: Exit findings map directly to Lucid: fixed dollar targets ($150-400/day on micros) and breakeven stops suit the payout-day and consistency rules; avoid ATR trailing stops.

strategies.name: Andrea Unger / Unger Academy: prior-session level re-cross and bias strategies on ES/GC
strategies.origin: Unger Academy blog 2023-2025 (post 102 fetchable; Oops, Crabel-on-Nasdaq, gold-bias and myths posts captcha-walled)
strategies.entry: Strategy 1 (ES, 15-min bars): long when a bar closes back above the previous session's low after trading below it; short when it closes back below the previous session's high. Strategy 2: limit buy at current session low minus an offset. Bias method [interp]: average open-to-close P&L by hour-of-day/day-of-week over 10+ years, trade the recurring window with a time stop.
strategies.exit: Strategy 1: stop $1,300, target $4,000 per ES, exit at session end. Strategy 2: stop $800, target $3,000, session-end exit. Day-trade translation: 0.5 x ATR stop, prior-close target, flat 15:55.
strategies.filters: Undisclosed extra filters 'especially on the short side'.
strategies.parameters: 15-min bars; dollar stops/targets above; offset optimized.
strategies.timeframe_session: RTH 15-min bars, session-end exit
strategies.claimed_performance: Strategy 1: ~750 trades over 6-7 yrs incl. OOS, avg ~$300/trade, 2022 +$15k, 2023 +$18k per ES. Strategy 2: ~1,800 trades, avg ~$140, 2020 +$40k, 2023 +$33k. No slippage disclosure.
strategies.prop_fit: Low-win-rate big-target shape hurts consistency; use the re-cross trigger with tighter stop/target. Time-of-day biases on GC are directly testable on our 1-min data.

strategies.name: Art Collins: combined small biases (fade two same-way open-to-closes, 15-day high-low average, day-of-week)
strategies.origin: Art Collins (with Robert Pardo), Beating the Financial Futures Market (Wiley 2006); Better System Trader ep. 73; Scribd TOC
strategies.entry: Daily open-to-close trades: fade two same-way open-to-closes (both last two days closed above their opens -> sell the open; both below -> buy the open); 15-day high-low average (buy the open when yesterday's close > 15-day average of (H+L)/2, sell when below); day-of-week (long bias early in the week in S&P); open-vs-prior-close; score biases +1/-1 and trade when the net score exceeds a threshold.
strategies.exit: Exit on the close (no intraday stop in the book).
strategies.filters: Four optimization rules: good neighbourhood, works across S&P/Russell/Nasdaq, profits spread through time, hypothesis stated first.
strategies.parameters: 15-day average; 2-day same-way count; score threshold.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily, open-to-close (09:30-16:00 ET)
strategies.claimed_performance: Book tables (not retrievable); no modern OOS.
strategies.prop_fit: Stop-less open-to-close holds expose the account to the full daily range ($2,500-4,000 per ES mini on bad days) -> can breach the $2,000 intraday floor; use in 1-3 micros or as a directional filter for intraday systems.
strategies.data_requirements: Daily OHLC (Yahoo) for scores; 1-min for execution

strategies.name: John Ehlers: roofing-filter anticipatory stochastic, PDF-inferred RSI/Fisher strategies, MAMA/FAMA
strategies.origin: Ehlers, mesasoftware.com papers: MAMA (2001), Predictive Indicators (2013), Inferring Trading Strategies from PDFs (2008), Robustness procedure
strategies.entry: (a) Roofing filter = 2-pole high-pass (48-bar) + SuperSmoother (10-bar), stochastic of the filtered series; buy when it crosses BELOW 20% (anticipating the trough), short when it crosses ABOVE 80% (confirmation entries lose). (b) Generic RSI and High-pass+Fisher-transform strategies: sell short when the smoothed signal crosses above the upper threshold, buy when it crosses below the lower; reverse the position if adverse excursion exceeds a set % of entry price. (c) MAMA/FAMA: price (H+L)/2, Hilbert homodyne period, alpha = FastLimit/DeltaPhase bounded [0.05, 0.5], FAMA uses alpha/2; long on MAMA crossing above FAMA.
strategies.exit: Opposite signal; adverse-excursion reversal; intraday flat 15:55. Robustness: genetic optimisation (pop 40, keep 2,000 tests), median/max net-profit ratio (~75%) as expected OOS retention.
strategies.filters: Roofing band 10-48 bars removes aliasing noise and spectral dilation.
strategies.parameters: HP 48, SS 10, stochastic ~20, thresholds 0.2/0.8; FastLimit 0.5, SlowLimit 0.05; adverse-excursion % tuned (suggest 0.4 x ATR intraday).
strategies.instruments: S&P daily futures (10 yrs), US T-bond futures (5 yrs to 2007-12), 100 stocks 1998-2001
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily in the papers; 5-min RTH adaptation proposed
strategies.claimed_performance: Bonds 5 yrs, 1 contract, no costs: Channel $54,968 / 142 trades / 53.5% / PF 1.72 / DD $15,520; RSI $72,468 / 119 / 57.1% / PF 2.05 / DD $11,625; Fisher $73,125 / 135 / 57.0% / PF 2.10 / DD $9,125; MC annual: RSI $17,085 profit vs $6,219 DD, 96.6% P(>=breakeven). MAMA: 1,317 trades, 37.5% wins, $4.86/share avg vs $0.30 costs. Roofed-stochastic anticipatory on S&P daily: equity curve 'consistent winners' (no table).
strategies.prop_fit: Anticipatory oscillator with adverse-excursion reversal is a natural 5-min ES mean-reversion engine (57% wins, PF ~2 in his data), small stops, several trades/day, EOD flat; MAMA/FAMA too slow intraday. Highest-priority Ehlers item.

strategies.name: Welles Wilder: DMI/ADX crossover with extreme-point rule, Parabolic SAR, RSI, Volatility System
strategies.origin: Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978); TradingView ADX page
strategies.entry: DMI 14: +DM = H-H[1] if > L[1]-L and > 0; +DI/-DI = 100 x Wilder-smoothed DM / ATR; ADX = smoothed |+DI - -DI|/(+DI + -DI) x 100. Buy when +DI crosses above -DI with ADX > 25 (20-25 indeterminate); stop = extreme point (low of the crossover bar); signal persists on re-cross unless the extreme point is breached. Parabolic SAR: SAR += AF x (EP - SAR), AF 0.02 step to 0.20, stop-and-reverse. RSI 14 30/70. Volatility System: SAR at significant close +/- 3 x ATR(7).
strategies.exit: Extreme-point stop; SAR reversal; ARC reversal.
strategies.filters: ADX > 25 trend filter.
strategies.parameters: 14 periods; AF 0.02/0.20; ARC 3 x ATR(7).
strategies.timeframe_session: Any
strategies.claimed_performance: Historical; modern tests only on Indian equities / SPX option overlays (sibling report); no ES intraday net evidence.
strategies.prop_fit: ADX as a trend-day vs rotation filter is the useful piece; SAR/DMI crossover systems whipsaw intraday and Davey ranks parabolic exits below dollar targets.

strategies.name: Charles LeBeau: Chandelier exit, Yo-Yo exit, ADX filter
strategies.origin: LeBeau & Lucas, Technical Traders Guide to Computer Analysis of the Futures Market (1992) [book]
strategies.entry: Exits/filters rather than entries: trend systems only when ADX(14) > 20 and rising; counter-trend when ADX falls from above 30. 25x25 bond system: enter when close > close 25 days ago with ADX rising [approx].
strategies.exit: Chandelier = highest high since entry - 3 x ATR(22) (2.5-4 x); Yo-Yo = yesterday's close - 2 x ATR re-anchored each bar.
strategies.filters: ADX rising/falling.
strategies.parameters: ATR 22 x 3; Yo-Yo 2 x ATR; ADX 14 > 20.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily; Yo-Yo on 5-min as intraday disaster stop
strategies.claimed_performance: None modern; Davey's study ranks chandelier below dollar targets.
strategies.prop_fit: Exits only; Yo-Yo (close - 2 x ATR on 5-min) is a reasonable volatility-scaled disaster stop.

strategies.name: David Bean / Capstone ES-NQ gap-fill, gap-continuation and open-range day-trade systems
strategies.origin: David Bean, Seven Trading Systems for the S&P Futures (2010, EasyLanguage disclosed); Capstone Trading Systems product pages (hypothetical, 1 contract, no slippage disclosed)
strategies.entry: Four gap types [book]: open above yesterday's high; inside range above close; inside range below close; below yesterday's low. Gap Fill fades toward the prior close with a PT/SL ratio (ES GAPF I enters 09:32 ET); Gap Continuation enters in the gap direction when early momentum aligns (NQ, long only in the 2020 version); ES Mirror 2020 enters long at 09:31 ET; NQ Open Range 2026 breaks the opening range; NQ GAPC 2024 trades 10:30-15:30.
strategies.exit: Fixed dollar stops/targets: ES Mirror stop $525 / target $675; Gap Continuation NQ max loss $1,225 (~49 NQ pts), exits by 15:30; GAPF I '700 PT / 500 SL'.
strategies.filters: Gap type classification; early-momentum alignment (undisclosed).
strategies.parameters: Entry 09:31-09:32 ET (ES systems); stop $1,225 NQ ($122 MNQ); PT/SL ratio.
strategies.timeframe_session: RTH day trades, 09:30-15:30/16:00 ET
strategies.prop_fit: NQ continuation shape (57-60% wins, win/loss ~1.3, $122 MNQ stop) is prop-friendly in micros; ES gap-fill shape (avg loss > avg win, PF 1.21) has decayed; open-range 37% win rate with $2,213 avg winners is wrong for the 50% consistency rule. Vendor re-releases systems yearly (survivorship).
strategies.data_requirements: OHLC; gap definitions need the RTH prior close (16:00 settlement vs 16:15 close)

strategies.name: Howard Bandy: short-horizon mean reversion and CAR25 / safe-f framework
strategies.origin: Bandy, Mean Reversion Trading Systems (2013), Quantitative Technical Analysis (2015); Better System Trader ep. 61, 6
strategies.entry: [book, standard form] daily equities/ETFs: buy at the close when z-score(close vs 20-day mean) < -1.5 or RSI(2) < 10.
strategies.exit: Sell at the close when z > 0 / RSI(2) > 70 or after 3-5 days; no stops (stops hurt in his tests).
strategies.filters: Benchmark for a competitive system: >= 65% accuracy, 1-2 day holds, 20-40 trades/yr; risk defined by account size, 2-yr horizon, 20% max DD at 5% probability.
strategies.parameters: CAR25 = 25th-percentile compound return from Monte Carlo; safe-f = position fraction meeting the DD constraint.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily, multi-day
strategies.claimed_performance: Author tests on equities; no numbers published in fetched sources.
strategies.prop_fit: Multi-day equity reversion not tradable; CAR25/safe-f and the 65%-accuracy short-hold benchmark are directly reusable for the Monte-Carlo monthly-pass-rate engine.

strategies.name: Brent Penfold: 1-5 bar price patterns validated on a 24-market universal portfolio
strategies.origin: Penfold, The Universal Principles of Successful Trading (2010); Better System Trader ep. 101
strategies.entry: Daily OHLC bar sequences 1-5 bars long; example key reversal: today opens below yesterday's close, makes a higher high, closes below yesterday's close -> sell next day below the low.
strategies.exit: Stop beyond the pattern bar; short/medium/long-term versions [book].
strategies.filters: Pattern must show positive expectancy across all 24 markets (P24) before use; no indicator parameters.
strategies.parameters: None (pattern definitions only).
strategies.instruments: 24-market portfolio: currencies, rates, indices, energies, metals, softs, grains, meats
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily, next-day stop entry
strategies.claimed_performance: No numbers published.
strategies.prop_fit: Same shape as Smash Day/Whiplash (low frequency, range-sized stops); the cross-market acceptance test is a good robustness criterion for ES/NQ/GC.

strategies.name: Jake Bernstein: 30-minute breakout and gap methods (The Compleat Day Trader)
strategies.origin: Bernstein, The Compleat Day Trader (1995/2007) [book]
strategies.entry: 30-min breakout: range of 09:30-10:00 ET; buy stop above / sell stop below. Gap method: open gaps beyond yesterday's close and trades back through the open toward the fill -> fade the gap toward yesterday's close. MACD/momentum divergence timing; day-of-week/seasonal filters.
strategies.exit: Stop at the opposite side of the 30-min range (or beyond the day's extreme for the gap fade); exit at the close.
strategies.filters: Day-of-week/seasonal.
strategies.parameters: 30-min range; gap size thresholds unspecified.
strategies.timeframe_session: RTH day trade
strategies.claimed_performance: Book tables only; the ORB-30 family is covered by modern studies in the sibling ORB report (close-confirmed ORB-30 with 0.25-0.5x range targets among the best-shaped).
strategies.prop_fit: Covered under ORB-30 in orb_session.md.

strategies.name: Murray Ruggiero: report-day fade, intermarket bond/S&P filter, adaptive channel breakout
strategies.origin: Ruggiero, Cybernetic Trading Strategies (1997); Better System Trader ep. 42
strategies.entry: Report-day: sell a strong pre-report rally / buy a strong pre-report sell-off (traders overreact before announcements). Intermarket: directional filter from a moving-average cross of the related market (T-bonds for S&P; utilities for bonds; XAU for gold); divergence = mean-reversion trade; relationships invert at 2.6 standard deviations. Adaptive channel breakout: channel length = measured dominant cycle.
strategies.exit: Not specified in fetched sources.
strategies.filters: Robustness: average net profit across the parameter grid >= 2 x its std dev, profitable across the whole range.
strategies.parameters: 2.6 sigma inversion threshold; MA lengths per pair.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily; report days (08:30/10:00/14:00 ET releases)
strategies.claimed_performance: 'Won 63% of report day trades' (interview claim); no modern OOS.
strategies.prop_fit: Intermarket filters codeable from Yahoo daily ZB/ZN vs ES; report-day rule needs an economic calendar (not available) - only approximable with fixed release times.
strategies.data_requirements: Daily cross-market data (Yahoo); economic release calendar (NOT available - flag)

strategies.name: Thomas Stridsman: Meander system (volatility-band open fade)
strategies.origin: Stridsman, Trading Systems That Work (2000) [book, approximate]
strategies.entry: Over the last 5 days compute % distance of each O/H/L/C from the previous close (20 observations), mean m and std s; band = yesterday's close x (1 + m +/- s). Buy the open if it is below the lower band (unusually weak open); sell the open if above the upper band.
strategies.exit: Exit on the close (day trade) or next open; no stop originally, later versions add 1-2 x ATR.
strategies.filters: None.
strategies.parameters: 5-day window; 1 standard deviation band.
strategies.timeframe_session: Daily open-to-close
strategies.claimed_performance: Book tests 1990s, modest positive; no modern test.
strategies.prop_fit: Volatility-normalised cousin of Oops/80-20/gap fades; include as a parameterisation of the gap-fade family with a stop at the day's extreme.
